security_spec.violation_condition: Linux kernel context-switches between tasks while Sscsrind is active (any extension using siselect/sireg* indirect CSR access is present), without saving and restoring siselect or sireg* in __switch_to or the entry.S trap context-save path. Task A sets siselect to select a specific indirect register window; preemption occurs; task B reads sireg* and observes the register state selected by task A's residual siselect value. Currently arch/riscv/kernel/entry.S and arch/riscv/kernel/process.c __switch_to save sstatus/sepc/stvec/sscratch but never touch siselect (CSR 0x150) or sireg* (CSR 0x151-0x157).
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: context switch save/restore list missing siselect or sireg; switch_to without siselect save; grep for CSR_SISELECT or CSR_SIREG in arch/riscv/kernel/entry.S and arch/riscv/kernel/process.c returning no hits versus their definitions in arch/riscv/include/asm/csr.h at 0x150-0x157; indirect CSR window selector not in thread_struct
security_spec.summary: siselect/sireg* are not saved/restored on context switch: any extension using Sscsrind leaks register state across task boundaries via residual siselect window selection

findings.finding: __switch_to saves/restores callee-saved GPRs (ra, sp, s0-s11) and the SUM bit from sstatus, but never saves or restores siselect (CSR 0x150) or any sireg* CSR (0x151-0x157). If the hart implements Sscsrind, these CSRs exist as architectural supervisor state. Any siselect value set before a context switch persists into the next task, allowing task B to observe indirect register state through the window selected by task A's residual siselect value. Similarly, sireg2-sireg6 (0x152-0x153, 0x155-0x157) are entirely absent from the kernel's CSR definitions in csr.h, which only defines CSR_SIREG (0x151) but not CSR_SIREG2 through CSR_SIREG6.
findings.snippet:
SYM_FUNC_START(__switch_to)
	li    a4,  TASK_THREAD_RA
	add   a3, a0, a4
	add   a4, a1, a4
	REG_S ra,  TASK_THREAD_RA_RA(a3)
	[... no siselect/sireg save/restore ...]
	REG_L s11, TASK_THREAD_S11_RA(a4)
	move tp, a1
	scs_load_current
	ret

spec_citations.excerpt: Supervisor-level CSRs: siselect 0x150 (SRW), sireg 0x151 (SRW), sireg2 0x152 (SRW), sireg3 0x153 (SRW), sireg4 0x155 (SRW), sireg5 0x156 (SRW), sireg6 0x157 (SRW). The CSRs in the table above are required if S-mode is implemented.

findings.finding: The trap entry path (handle_exception) saves sstatus, sepc, stval, scause, sscratch to the pt_regs frame but does not save siselect (0x150) or any sireg* (0x151-0x157). If a trap occurs while siselect holds a non-default value (set by kernel code or by an extension-dependent store), that value is not preserved across the trap handler. The ret_from_exception path (line 247-317) restores sstatus and sepc from pt_regs but never touches siselect/sireg*.
findings.snippet:
.Lsave_context:
	REG_S sp, TASK_TI_USER_SP(tp)
	REG_L sp, TASK_TI_KERNEL_SP(tp)
	addi sp, sp, -(PT_SIZE_ON_STACK)
	[... saves x1,x3,x5-x31, sstatus,sepc,stval,scause,sscratch ...]
	csrw CSR_SCRATCH, x0

spec_citations.excerpt: siselect (0x150) and sireg* (0x151-0x157) are supervisor-level CSRs required if S-mode is implemented under Sscsrind.

findings.finding: thread_struct has no fields for siselect or any sireg* register. Without storage in the per-task thread struct, context-switch save/restore of these CSRs is impossible. Compare with envcfg (line 113) and sum (line 114) which are properly stored per-task. A siselect field would be needed to save the indirect register window selector across context switches.

spec_citations.excerpt: Attempts to access sireg* from M-mode or S-mode while siselect holds a number in a standard-defined and implemented range result in specific behavior that, for each combination of siselect and sireg_i, is defined by the extension to which the siselect value is allocated.

findings.finding: The switch_to macro handles FPU save/restore, vector save/restore, icache flush, and envcfg restore, but has no call to save/restore siselect or sireg*. The pattern for envcfg (__switch_to_envcfg on line 124) shows how per-task CSR state should be handled during context switch; siselect, being analogous supervisor architectural state that controls which indirect register window is active, needs equivalent treatment.

spec_citations.excerpt: The siselect register will support the value range 0..0xFFF at a minimum. [...] Values of siselect with the most-significant bit set (bit XLEN - 1 = 1) are designated only for custom use.

findings.finding: Only CSR_SISELECT (0x150) and CSR_SIREG (0x151) are defined. The spec defines seven supervisor-level CSRs for Sscsrind: siselect (0x150), sireg (0x151), sireg2 (0x152), sireg3 (0x153), sireg4 (0x155), sireg5 (0x156), sireg6 (0x157). CSR_SIREG2, CSR_SIREG3, CSR_SIREG4, CSR_SIREG5, CSR_SIREG6 are missing. Note that 0x154 is already used for CSR_SIPH (AIA), and sireg4-sireg6 (0x155-0x157) similarly have no definitions. Any future kernel code that needs to access these registers will need the definitions added.

spec_citations.excerpt: Supervisor-level CSRs: siselect 0x150, sireg 0x151, sireg2 0x152, sireg3 0x153, sireg4 0x155, sireg5 0x156, sireg6 0x157.

findings.finding: The kernel's ISA extension table does not include Sscsrind, Ssccfg, Smcdeleg, Smctr, or Ssctr. None of the extensions that depend on the Sscsrind indirect CSR access mechanism are detected or advertised. This means the kernel is unaware of whether the hardware implements Sscsrind and treats siselect/sireg* CSRs as non-existent. This is the root cause of the missing context-switch handling: the kernel cannot conditionally save/restore CSRs for an extension it doesn't know exists.

spec_citations.excerpt: The machine-level extension Smcsrind encompasses all added CSRs and all behavior modifications for a hart, over all privilege levels. For a supervisor-level environment, extension Sscsrind is essentially the same as Smcsrind except excluding the machine-level CSRs and behavior not directly visible to supervisor level.
Smctr and Ssctr depend on both the implementation of S-mode and the Sscsrind extension.

findings.finding: KVM's AIA IMSIC code correctly saves and restores vsiselect around IMSIC indirect register accesses (e.g., lines 380/419). The pattern `old_vsiselect = csr_read(CSR_VSISELECT); ... csr_write(CSR_VSISELECT, old_vsiselect);` demonstrates the correct save/restore discipline needed for indirect CSR selectors. This same pattern is missing from the non-KVM context-switch paths (__switch_to, handle_exception).

spec_citations.excerpt: vsiselect (0x250) and vsireg* (0x251-0x257) are the virtual supervisor-level indirect CSR access CSRs.

findings.finding: KVM's AIA VCPU code properly saves vsiselect to per-VCPU storage (csr->vsiselect) during VCPU load/put. This is the correct pattern for virtualizing the indirect CSR selector across VCPU switches. The absence of equivalent siselect handling in the non-virtualized context-switch path (__switch_to, switch_to macro) is the gap.

spec_citations.excerpt: Virtual Supervisor-level CSRs: vsiselect (0x250), vsireg (0x251), vsireg2-6. These CSRs are required if the hypervisor extension is implemented.
